title: Deterministic model selection: pinning semantics for tags, semver ranges, and commit ids
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement:

We need a deterministic, easy-to-understand, and backward-compatible model resolution behavior across the Redwood API and SDKs so customers can reliably pin model variants for production traffic. Current onboarding artifacts and early SDK versions accept several identifier formats (human tags, semantic version ranges, and raw source commit ids) but the resolution precedence, compatibility checks, and failure modes are underspecified. This ticket defines the semantics, example API payloads, SDK convenience helpers, and the publishing contract for associated performance profiles.

Goals:
- Define canonical pin forms: tag (user-defined label), semver (exact or range), and commit id (git SHA-like opaque identifier).
- Specify deterministic resolution precedence and tie-break rules across multiple matching candidates.
- Ensure performance profiles published with a model version are discoverable and bound to the resolved version id.
- Design API and SDK ergonomics for pinning that are clear, minimally surprising, and upgrade-friendly.
- Outline migration guidance for customers using older free-form pins.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement the server-side rollout mechanism or canary policies (those are separate). It only specifies resolution semantics and SDK surface changes required to pin models deterministically.
resolution_semantics:
High-level rules (deterministic algorithm):

1) Exact commit pins: if type=commit and the specified id exists, resolution returns that specific immutable version. This is highest precedence (no other candidate considered).

2) Exact semver: if type=semver and value is an exact version (no range operators), match exact version if present. If absent, fail with a clear 409 + resolution_suggestions payload.

3) Semver ranges: evaluate all model versions that include semantic metadata and satisfy the range. From the candidate set, choose the version with the highest semver precedence. If there are multiple build variants with identical semver (rare), apply deterministic tie-break: prefer the version with the latest published_at timestamp; if still tied, prefer canonical build with smallest hash lexicographically.

4) Tags: tags are user-maintained pointers that may point to one or more versions (for multi-variant tags). When a tag maps to multiple candidates: apply the tag's configured stability policy (tag metadata: "pinned" vs "floating"). For "pinned" tags, tag resolves to an immutable version id recorded at tag creation time. For "floating" tags, tag resolves to the best semver candidate per rule (3). If tag metadata is missing, treat as floating for backward compatibility.

5) Mixed inputs: if user passes multiple pins (e.g., {tag: X, semver_range: Y}), server must return 400 — require a single canonical pin. SDK helpers should validate and throw early errors.

6) Failure modes and HTTP responses:
- 404 Model not found when no model family matches the requested handle.
- 409 Ambiguous resolution when multiple disjoint candidates match but server cannot determine preference; include resolution candidates in response body.
- 422 Invalid pin format when semver parsing fails or commit id length/charset invalid.

7) Compatibility constraints: semver-range pins are considered compatible with performance profiles only if the resolved version has a performance profile published with matching ABI/quantization/sequence_length buckets. If a profile mismatch exists, server should return 409 with a "profile_mismatch" code and suggested fallbacks.
sdk_behavior_and_helpers:
SDK responsibilities and convenience APIs:

- Provide typed helpers: ModelPin.tag('stable-2026-03'), ModelPin.semver('1.4.2'), ModelPin.range('^1.4.0'), ModelPin.commit('3f9d...').
- Local validation: SDK will validate formats (semver syntax, commit length) and refuse to send invalid pins.
- Resolve-on-demand helper: sdk.resolvePin(pin) -> returns same resolved_model structure as server for offline checks. This is a thin wrapper that calls API but provides nicer typed results.
- Retry/backoff: SDK should optionally accept fallback policies for semver-ranges (e.g., fallbackToLatestPatch=true).
- Surface resolved_model in route and request objects so users can log canonical version ids for observability and audits.

Backward compatibility: older SDKs that accept string pins will be mapped server-side into a best-effort pin type (heuristics: full SHA => commit, number-dot-number => semver). We will encourage customers to migrate to typed helpers via a deprecation warning in SDK 1.0 -> 1.2 releases.
performance_profile_publishing_contract:
When a model version is published, it must be accompanied by zero-or-more performance profiles. Each profile must include metadata fields: version_id (canonical), quantization (e.g., fp16, int8), kernel_config_tag, sequence_length_buckets, measured_tokens_per_sec, p50/p95 latency for representative prompt sizes, and measured_cost_estimate.

Server guarantees:
- Profiles are indexed by version_id and by model_family+semver for quick lookups.
- When resolving a semver-range or floating tag, server will attempt to select a candidate version with a matching performance profile for the requested runtime options (quantization, kernel selection). If none exists, response includes "profile_suggestion" array listing nearest compatible versions.

SDK will expose an endpoint: client.models.listPerformanceProfiles(model_family, filter) that returns human-readable comparators so customers can decide which pin to prefer for cost/latency tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Server exposes deterministic resolution algorithm matching documented precedence (commit > exact semver > semver-range > tag-floating > tag-pinned resolved id)
API returns resolved_model with canonical version id on route creation and inference responses
SDK provides typed ModelPin helpers and performs client-side validation
Conflict and mismatch cases return documented HTTP codes and structured suggestions
Performance profiles are discoverable and associated with canonical version ids; semver-range resolution prefers candidates with matching profiles when requested
testing_and_migration_plan:
Tests to add:
- Unit tests for resolution logic with synthetic version sets covering edge cases (same semver different builds, identical timestamps, tag pointing to multiple versions).
- Integration tests: create model family, publish versions + profiles, exercise pin types and validate resolved_model output.
- Backward compatibility smoke: old string-pin formats map to expected pin types.

Migration notes for customers:
- Deprecate free-form string pins over 3 releases. Announce via console banner and email.
- Provide a migration tool that lists current routes using ambiguous pins and suggests explicit replacements (commit or semver).

Rollout:
- Feature gated behind runtime-1.22 for 2 weeks in staging, then opt-in in dedicated clusters, then default on Hosted API after monitoring 7 days of traffic for any 4xx spikes related to pin resolution.
